shape.description: What the part is, structurally: the outline, the openings, how many solids and which parameter is the thickness. Never where anything is - coordinates are the compilation stage's job. This is checked against the compiled CAD-IR by trusted code, so a misread outline is caught before a valid document that builds the wrong part reaches anyone.

profile.description: The outline of the part. Use closed_profile when the outline is not one of the named shapes; never pick the nearest named one.

openings.description: Holes and cut-outs, grouped by the shape of the opening and by whether they go through. Count every one the drawing shows. Empty when the part has none.

through.description: true when the drawing shows these going all the way through, false when they stop inside the material, null when it does not say. Guessing is worse than null: a depth nobody stated is the one thing no later check can recover.

solids.description: How many separate solid bodies of material the part is made of: one for a plain plate, two for a plate with a boss standing on it.

thickness_parameter.description: The id of the parameter above that holds the part's depth, or null when the drawing does not give one. Naming it is what keeps the dimension a name rather than a number.

wall_parameter.description: The id of the parameter holding the wall thickness when the part is hollow - a box, a housing, a cover with a wall rather than solid material - and null when it is solid or the drawing does not say. A hollow part and a solid one of the same size agree on every other field here and differ by several times the material, so this is the only thing that catches a part built solid.

blends.description: Rounded and chamfered edges the drawing marks, grouped by kind and counted. A corner radius note that applies to all four corners is one entry with count 4. Empty when the drawing marks none.

note.description: What the outline is, in words, when profile is closed_profile. Read by a person, never by a check.

steps.description: How many distinct outside sizes the part has along its axis, read off a sectional view. A plain plate or cylinder is 1; a flanged bushing is 2; a bushing with a flange and a reduced nose is 3. Null when the drawing does not settle it - silence agrees with whatever gets built. A count, never a size.

parameter_id.description: The parameter this question is about, or the literal "shape" when the question is about the outline or the openings rather than a number.

answer_kind.description: What an answer to this question is. A question the reading stage can ask but the customer cannot answer is a dead end, and until this existed every question was rendered as a number field with a mm suffix — so "is this opening through or blind?" had no answer that would be accepted. Ask one question per value: two numbers are two questions, not one answer.

choices.description: The answers offered, for answer_kind "choice". Empty for "number". Required rather than optional because the Codex dialect has no optional properties (ADR-029 rule 4); an empty array is how a number question says it offers none.
